hero.headline: Bomb squad, FBI respond to Fort Pierce home after suspected devices found
hero.teaser: The bomb squad, FBI agents, and federal Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco and Firearms agents surrounded a Fort Pierce home Thursday after St. Lucie County sheriff's deputies discovered s
hero.body:
The bomb squad, FBI agents, and federal Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco and Firearms agents surrounded a Fort Pierce home Thursday after St. Lucie County sheriff's deputies discovered suspected destructive devices while serving a risk protection order. One person was detained pending investigation.

 Deputies went to a home in the 6000 block of Balsam Drive around 12:20 p.m. Thursday to serve a risk protection order, a legal order temporarily restricting someone from possessing firearms. When deputies entered the home, they found a box of items that were indicative of being destructive devices, said Capt. Bolonka of the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office.

 Deputies backed out of the home, called the bomb squad, and notified federal authorities. The bomb squad secured the items in the back of the bomb disposal vehicle. Investigators did not disclose what the destructive devices were.

 Terry Rates, who has lived in the neighborhood for ten years, described the area as peaceful and said he was surprised by the law enforcement activity. "It's a really nice neighborhood. That's the first I've ever heard of anything happening around here," he said.

hero.headline: Bomb squad, FBI respond to Fort Pierce home after suspected devices found
hero.teaser: The bomb squad, FBI agents, and federal Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco and Firearms agents surrounded a Fort Pierce home Thursday after St. Lucie County sheriff's deputies discovered s
hero.body:
The bomb squad, FBI agents, and federal Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco and Firearms agents surrounded a Fort Pierce home Thursday after St. Lucie County sheriff's deputies discovered suspected destructive devices while serving a risk protection order. One person was detained pending investigation.

 Deputies went to a home in the 6000 block of Balsam Drive around 12:20 p.m. Thursday to serve a risk protection order, a legal order temporarily restricting someone from possessing firearms. When deputies entered the home, they found a box of items that were indicative of being destructive devices, said Capt. Bolonka of the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office.

 Deputies backed out of the home, called the bomb squad, and notified federal authorities. The bomb squad secured the items in the back of the bomb disposal vehicle. Investigators did not disclose what the destructive devices were.

 Terry Rates, who has lived in the neighborhood for ten years, described the area as peaceful and said he was surprised by the law enforcement activity. "It's a really nice neighborhood. That's the first I've ever heard of anything happening around here," he said.
